claim: Hands-on workshops engage participants more actively and yield higher knowledge retention than passive sessions; 77% of attendees say interactive elements improved their experience.
quote: workshops engage participants more actively, leading to higher knowledge retention than passive sessions. 77% of conference attendees reported that interactive elements improved their event experience.

claim: Break the passive-listening pattern with quick engagement checkpoints every 10-12 minutes.
quote: Breaking the passive listening pattern regularly through quick engagement checkpoints every 10-12 minutes is key.

claim: Plan breaks strategically (after-lunch slump), insert energisers, and use a co-facilitator to maintain stamina; 90-minute modules outperform half-day marathons.
quote: In AI onboarding sessions, 90-minute modules with short breaks yield more focus than half-day marathons.

claim: Typical session length has shortened from half a day to 90 minutes; blended in-person + online touchpoints and co-facilitation ('four eyes see more than two') are emphasised.
quote: blended programs combining high-impact in-person workshops with ongoing online touchpoints ... four eyes see more than two

claim: Live-coding survival: store states in git branches so you can jump forward if something breaks; keep a backup screen-recording for catastrophic failure; avoid relying on connectivity; maximise font/contrast and test from the back of the room.
quote: store different states in version control through branches ... if something goes wrong during your talk, you can still switch to a further state

claim: Don't type from scratch; prepare most of the program upfront, paste boring chunks, and automate reset with 'git reset --hard && git clean -fdx'.
quote: automate resetting all the files you need back to the desired state, using git reset --hard && git clean -fdx

claim: Tools like Demo Time replay scripted keystrokes so a live demo runs with no typos or missteps.
quote: execute flawless demos with simple keyboard shortcuts and no typos, no missteps, or stress

claim: A real 2026 MCP workshop sets prerequisites as Node.js 18+, VS Code, a GitHub account with Copilot, plus pre-created API credentials, with a 'node --version' pre-flight check.
quote: Node.js 18+ ... Run the following command to confirm Node.js compatibility: node --version. Expected output: v18.x.x or higher

claim: Duke's Innovation Co-Lab runs a 2-hour interactive 'Building MCP Servers' workshop (build your first MCP server), recommending basic Python/OOP familiarity.
quote: An interactive, beginner-friendly session designed to teach participants how to build your first Model Context Protocol (MCP) server

claim: Microsoft's MCP Dev Days schedules a 'Vibe Code your first MCP server' build session targeted at under 30 minutes, alongside watch-only keynotes and demos.
quote: Vibe Code your first MCP server with GitHub Copilot ... implement a server in less than 30 minutes

claim: The official MCP build-server tutorial walks a weather server exposing two tools (get_alerts, get_forecast), then connects it to a host; servers provide tools, resources, and prompts.
quote: We'll build a server that exposes two tools: get_alerts and get_forecast. Then we'll connect the server to an MCP host

claim: The official MCP TypeScript SDK is the reference implementation; build servers with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and Zod for schema validation.
quote: The official TypeScript SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients

claim: MCP Inspector is the official visual testing/debugging tool; it runs a stdio server as a child process and exposes a web UI at localhost:6274.
quote: Visual testing tool for MCP servers ... the UI will be accessible at http://localhost:6274

claim: Never log to stdout from a stdio server; log to stderr via console.error so Inspector renders it in the 'Server output' debug panel.
quote: You should never log to stdout from a stdio-transport server, and instead log to stderr via console.error

claim: A 2026 TypeScript MCP build typically goes: npm init, install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk + zod, define a tool, wire stdio transport, test in Inspector.
quote: Build an MCP Server with TypeScript: 2026 Tutorial

claim: Lock-file enforcement and 'npm ci' cut deployment failures dramatically; version mismatches are a leading cause of hard-to-debug integration failures.
quote: reduced deployment failures by 73% simply by enforcing lock file usage across teams and switching to npm ci

claim: Hallucinated/non-existent dependencies are a 2026 risk when blindly running AI-suggested npm/pip installs.
quote: Hallucinated Dependencies represent a major 2026 risk where AI models invent non-existent packages

claim: Conference workshops require attendees to bring a laptop with node, npm, git, and an editor installed beforehand.
quote: require attendees to bring a laptop with node, npm, git, and a code editor installed
